title: Spending policies: who and what can consume Copilot Credits, and up to how much
summary: The documented controls, policy-selection rules, billing order and monitoring behaviour support the page. Both API endpoints flagged by the automatic pre-check are present in Microsoft's reference, and the page explicitly acknowledges the conflicting License Administrator guidance.

claims.claim: Default-policy activation starts in Microsoft 365 admin center at Copilot > Cost Management > Get Started.
claims.quote:
In the Microsoft 365 admin center, go to **Copilot** and then the **Cost Management** node.
3. To unlock AI experiences enabled by usage-based billing, select **Get Started**.

claims.claim: Microsoft does not document an API equivalent for initial default-policy activation, distinct from creating an allUsersSpendingPolicy.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot costManagement activate default spending policy API allUsersSpendingPolicy PowerShell. Opened setup, Cost Management API overview and spendingpolicy-create; creation is documented, but no initial-activation operation or equivalence is stated.

claims.claim: Identity policies are created in Microsoft 365 admin center at Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > + Add spending policy.
claims.quote:
In the Microsoft 365 admin center, go to **Copilot > Cost Management**.
2. Select the **Configuration** tab and then select **+ Add spending policy**.

claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies creates an identity policy with @odata.type, displayName, periodLimit, perUserLimit and serviceSettings.
claims.quote:
POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies

Required properties are `displayName`, `periodLimit`, `perUserLimit`, and `serviceSettings`.

claims.claim: Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > policy > Save changes edits scope, services, billing method, limits and alerts.
claims.quote:
Select the **Configuration** tab.
3. Select the spending policy you want to edit.
4. The spending policy details fly-out opens, where you can modify its settings.

claims.claim: The beta spendingPolicies/{id} PATCH uses If-Match and updates only displayName, periodLimit, perUserLimit and billingMethods, not scope, services or alerts.
Policy alert settings are in the details fly-out at Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > policy.
claims.quote:
Select the spending policy you want to edit.
4. The spending policy details fly-out opens, where you can modify its settings. This includes:
    1. **Scope**
    2. **Agents and services**
    3. **Billing method**
    4. **Spending limits**

claims.claim: PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/{id}/emailThresholdSettings configures policy alert thresholds.

claims.claim: Copilot Studio resource policies are created at Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > Add spending policy, choosing Resources.
claims.quote:
In the Microsoft 365 admin center, go to **Copilot > Cost Management**.
2. Select **Configuration**, and then select **Add spending policy**.
3. Enter a name for the policy, then select **Resources** as its scope.

claims.claim: No Graph call for resource-based Copilot Studio spending policies is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "resource-based" "spending" "API"; "spending policies" "resource" "Graph" PowerShell. Opened Studio costs, API overview and create reference; read spendingPolicy search excerpts. Graph documents only allUsersSpendingPolicy and selectedGroupsSpendingPolicy.

claims.claim: A policy is deleted from Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration using its More actions menu and Delete.
claims.quote:
From the list of spending policies, locate the spending policy that you want to delete.
4. Select the More actions menu (⋮) next to the spending policy.
5. Select **Delete**.

claims.claim: DELETE https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/{id} deletes a spending policy.
claims.quote: | [Delete spendingPolicy](spendingpolicy-delete) | DELETE `/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/{id}` | Delete a spending policy. |

claims.claim: Spending policies are administrator-defined access and credit-spending rules in Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: Use spending policies in the Cost Management dashboard to control access and Copilot Credit spending for AI experiences enabled by usage-based billing.

claims.claim: A spending policy selects which services may consume credits under it.
claims.quote: Use the check box to select the agents and services that can consume credits against the billing method tied to this policy.

claims.claim: A spending policy can set a monthly policy-wide credit limit.
claims.quote: **Limited monthly budget**: When you select a limited monthly budget, you limit the number of credits that this policy can spend each month.

claims.claim: A spending policy specifies the billing method used for its consumption.
claims.quote:
Select a billing method

By default, the field selects the billing method tied to the default spending policy.

claims.claim: Spending policies are limit-based controls, not credit reservations or allocations.
claims.quote: Spending policies are limit-based controls and don't reserve or allocate Copilot Credits to users or groups.

claims.where: What it is: Two kinds of policy
claims.claim: An identity-based policy follows the person using the selected service.
claims.quote: Use this option when you want a policy to apply to the people who use selected agents and services.

claims.where: What it is: Two kinds of policy
claims.claim: Identity policies can cover all users or specific groups.
claims.quote: By default, **All users** is selected. To target this rule to a subset of users, switch to **Specific groups** and select the directory group. You can also select multiple groups.

claims.where: What it is: Two kinds of policy
claims.claim: Identity policies support per-user limits.
claims.quote: Select monthly budget limits for users (optional). Use the toggle to select this option and to set a monthly limit for users to prevent a single person from spending all available credits.

claims.where: What it is: Two kinds of policy
claims.claim: A resource-based policy follows the agent or environment rather than the person using it.
claims.quote: Use this option when you want usage to follow an agent or environment rather than the identity of the person using it.

claims.where: What it is: Two kinds of policy
claims.claim: Resource policies can cover specific agents, specific environments or all environments.
claims.quote:
**Specific resources**: Choose Specific resources when particular agents need their own policy or billing method.

**Specific environments**: Choose Specific environments when you want to move and manage a limited set of environments first.

**All environments**

claims.where: What it is: Two kinds of policy
claims.claim: Resource policies support per-agent limits.
claims.quote: You can also set a per-agent limit so that no single agent covered by the policy uses more than the amount you specify.

claims.where: What it is: Two kinds of policy
claims.claim: An identity policy can govern a group using Cowork.
claims.quote: Use this option when you want a policy to apply to the people who use selected agents and services. For example, a group using Cowork.

claims.where: What it is: Two kinds of policy
claims.claim: Resource policies govern Copilot Studio agents and environments.
claims.quote: Manage Copilot Studio spending in the Microsoft 365 admin center by creating policies for environments or individual agents.

claims.where: What it is: Two kinds of policy
claims.claim: An identity-based spending policy cannot be converted into a resource-based policy.
claims.quote: You can't convert an existing identity-based policy into a resource-based policy.

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: Initial usage-based billing setup activates the default policy and unlocks gated AI experiences.
claims.quote: This section covers the initial setup steps to guide administrators through enabling usage-based billing and creating the first spending policy. This process activates AI experiences, like Cowork, that are gated by usage-based billing.

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: The default setup targets the whole organisation and all users.
claims.quote: The default setup targets your entire organization and all users. Optionally, you can customize the default spending policy to specific groups or change the services it governs

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: Additional policies have independent limits and do not inherit the tenant-level limit.
claims.quote: Each additional spending policy that you create has its own independent limit and doesn't inherit the tenant-level limit.

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: A per-user monthly limit is optional.
claims.quote: In the **Select the monthly spending limit for users (optional)** section, set a monthly limit for users to prevent a single person from spending all available credits.

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: Policy settings include alert thresholds.
claims.quote:
Configure policy-level alerts:

    - Specify the usage threshold for the policy.
    - Select the administrators or stakeholders who must receive email notifications when policy usage reaches the threshold.

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: Auto-apply new services is on by default.
claims.quote: By default, the **Auto-apply new services** toggle is selected for spending policies.

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: Auto-apply automatically adds future supported services and agents; turning it off requires manual review and addition.
claims.quote:
When the setting is on, newly supported Microsoft Copilot services and agents are automatically added to the policy.
    - When the setting is off, future services and agents aren't automatically included. Administrators must review and add the new services and agents to the policy.

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: When several identity policies cover a user for one service, the highest per-user limit takes priority.
claims.quote:
If a user is in more than one policy for the same service, the system assigns the user a policy based on the following order:

1. Highest per-user limit

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: A tie in per-user limits is resolved by the largest overall policy limit.
claims.quote:
1. Highest per-user limit
2. If tied, the largest overall policy limit

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: A remaining tie is resolved by the most recently created policy.
claims.quote: 3. If still tied, the most recently created policy

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: For overlap comparison, a missing per-user limit is replaced by the policy's overall limit.
claims.quote: If a policy doesn't have a per-user limit set, the system uses its overall policy limit as the per-user value for this comparison.

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: The selected identity policy applies in full rather than combining limits or settings across policies.
claims.quote: The chosen policy applies in full and settings from other policies aren't combined.

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: For covered Copilot Studio usage, Microsoft 365 admin center policies take precedence over Power Platform admin center controls.
claims.quote: If a spending policy in the Microsoft 365 admin center covers the environment or agent, its controls take precedence over the Power Platform admin center controls for that usage.

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: A Copilot Studio resource-based policy takes precedence over an identity-based policy.
claims.quote: **Resource-based policy before identity-based policy**. Within the Microsoft 365 admin center, a policy for the agent or its environment takes precedence over a policy for the person using the agent.

claims.claim: Microsoft asks administrators to set a per-user limit to prevent runaway spending by one individual.
claims.quote: Although this selection is optional, review and set this option for your organization to prevent runaway spending of Copilot Credits by one individual user.

claims.claim: Don't limit monthly spending allows unrestricted spending against the billing method, with no ceiling from that policy limit.
claims.quote: **Don't limit monthly spending** - Allows the policy to use credits against the organization's billing method without restrictions.

claims.claim: Copilot Studio resource-policy management is opt-in; existing Power Platform configuration remains until a resource policy covers the scope.
claims.quote: To opt in, create a Microsoft 365 admin center resource-based spending policy. Until then, your existing Power Platform admin center configuration remains in effect.

claims.claim: Creating a resource policy transfers covered credit management to Microsoft 365 admin center, replacing Power Platform allocations and linked billing plans.
claims.quote: For resources covered by the spending policy, Copilot Credit management moves to the Microsoft 365 admin center, replacing their Power Platform admin center capacity allocations and linked billing plans.

claims.claim: A policy is not a purchase; charges arise from actual Copilot Credit consumption.
claims.quote: Microsoft's usage-based billing model charges customers based on actual usage, measured in Copilot Credits.

claims.claim: Copilot Credit usage is billed to the subscription selected in the policy's billing method.
claims.quote: Copilot credits are billed to the subscription that you select in the billing method.

claims.claim: When credits for the selected subscription run out, usage continues on pay-as-you-go.
claims.quote: When credits run out for that subscription, usage automatically continues on a pay-as-you-go basis.

claims.claim: When prepaid capacity packs and a subscription with P3 are both selected, billing uses capacity packs, then P3, then pay-as-you-go.
claims.quote:
If you select both Prepaid Capacity packs and an Azure subscription with Copilot Credit Pre-purchase plan (P3), billing is applied in the following order to keep spending predictable:

- Prepaid Capacity packs
- Copilot Credit Pre-purchase plan (P3)
- Pay-as-you-go billing

claims.claim: Global Administrators and Billing Administrators can create spending policies.
claims.quote: At runtime, creating a policy also requires the Billing Administrator or Global Administrator directory role.

claims.claim: Global Administrators and Billing Administrators can set or override a policy's billing method.
claims.quote: Global administrator and Billing administrator roles can add, select, and change billing methods, and set billing methods in policies.

claims.claim: Different policy billing methods enable departmental billing.
claims.quote: This feature enables you to do departmental billing and vary billing methods for each group, department, or set of users.

claims.claim: Licensing depends on the covered service, and Cowork requires a Copilot licence.
claims.quote:
Depending on the service, organizations can use fixed licensing, the Copilot Credit Pre-purchase Plan (P3), pay-as-you-go billing, prepaid capacity packs, or supported combinations of these billing methods.

Cowork (Copilot license required)

claims.claim: The spending-policy pages do not publish per-service credit rates and instead direct readers to licensing guidance.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot spending policies credit rates pricing. Opened setup, manage credits, Studio costs and usage-based billing overview; they do not give service rates. Overview links the Copilot Credits Guide. Search found rates on the separate Studio Billing rates and management page.

claims.claim: Consumption shows estimated costs that might not match the bill.
claims.quote: **Cost**: The estimated cost of your AI usage in local currency, including negotiated rates. It includes usage paid for with prepaid credits and with pay-as-you-go, so it might not match your bill.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Hitting a limit
claims.claim: Users who hit a spending limit lose access to agents and services for the rest of the month.
claims.quote: When users hit the limit, they lose access to agents and services for the rest of the month until credits reset on the first of the month.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Hitting a limit
claims.claim: Credits reset on the first of the month.
claims.quote: until credits reset on the first of the month.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Hitting a limit
claims.claim: Users who reach their policy limit can request more credits.
claims.quote: When users reach their limit within a policy, they can request more credits but they don't default to other policies.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Hitting a limit
claims.claim: Reaching a limit does not cause fallback to another policy.
claims.quote: The system keeps the user on the assigned policy and doesn't reevaluate the user against other policies.

claims.where: Risks and limits: A per-user overrun
claims.claim: A running task that exceeds a per-user spending limit can complete.
claims.quote: Users in a group spending policy that exceed their per-user spending limit: If a running task exceeds the per-user limit, it can complete without interruption.

claims.where: Risks and limits: A per-user overrun
claims.claim: The documented excess per-user task usage does not count toward the policy limit.
claims.quote: The excess usage doesn't count toward the policy limit

claims.where: Risks and limits: A per-user overrun
claims.claim: Microsoft says the documented excess per-user usage is not billed, at Microsoft's sole discretion.
claims.quote: isn't billed (at Microsoft's sole discretion)

claims.where: Risks and limits: A per-user overrun
claims.claim: The documented excess usage is absent from consumed credits in Cost Management dashboards.
claims.quote: doesn't appear as consumed credits in the Cost Management dashboards (**Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Cost Management**).

claims.claim: Selecting All environments applies resource-policy management tenant-wide.
claims.quote: Selecting **All environments** makes this change for every environment in the tenant.

claims.claim: A newly linked environment can take up to 12 minutes to receive its resource policy.
claims.quote: When you create a policy: After you link an environment to a Microsoft 365 spending policy, allow up to 12 minutes for the new policy to apply.

claims.claim: Removing an environment or deleting its resource policy automatically restores the applicable Power Platform policy.
claims.quote: If you remove an environment from a spending policy or delete the resource-based spending policy, the applicable Power Platform admin center policy resumes for that environment automatically.

claims.claim: Resource-based policies do not apply to AI Builder features or their credits.
claims.quote: Resource-based policies created in the Microsoft 365 admin center don't apply to AI Builder features or the credits they consume.

claims.claim: Microsoft advises against moving resources that use AI Builder to resource-based spending policies.
claims.quote: Don't move resources, agents, workflows or environments that use AI Builder to these policies.

claims.claim: A user's prior consumption carries forward when group membership changes and counts against the new policy's limit.
claims.quote: Credits consumed under the previous spending policy remain part of the user's consumption history and are accounted for when enforcing the spending limit under the new policy. Moving a user between groups or spending policies doesn't reset the user's consumption.

claims.claim: The Consumption tab's user-level view displays only current usage against the current policy after a group move.
claims.quote: Only the current usage against the current spending policy is displayed at a user level in the Consumption tab view.

claims.claim: Coverage is defined by Microsoft's managed-service list, which Microsoft says it will expand.
claims.quote: For a list of services managed by usage-based billing method, see [Services managed by usage-based billing](../plan/usage-based-billing-overview-copilot-credits#services-managed-by-usage-based-billing). Microsoft is working to bring more agents and services to be managed by this experience.

claims.claim: Microsoft directs readers to a separate pay-as-you-go overview for Copilot Chat, SharePoint agents and the Retrieval API.
claims.quote: For Copilot Chat, SharePoint Agents, or Microsoft Copilot Retrieval API (Preview), see [Microsoft Copilot pay-as-you-go service overview](../plan/pay-as-you-go-overview).

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risks and limits: The API
claims.claim: The documented policy API is beta, subject to change and unsupported in production.
claims.quote: APIs under the `/beta` version are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risks and limits: The API
claims.claim: Policy operations support delegated work or school permissions, not application permissions.
claims.quote:
| Delegated (work or school account) | CopilotCostManagement-Policy.ReadWrite.All | Not supported. |
| Delegated (personal Microsoft account) | Not supported. | Not supported. |
| Application | Not supported. | Not supported. |

claims.claim: A policy created through Graph starts disabled.
claims.quote: A new policy is created `disabled`.

claims.claim: The Graph create operation requires the Billing Administrator or Global Administrator directory role at runtime.
claims.quote: At runtime, creating a policy also requires the Billing Administrator or Global Administrator directory role.

claims.claim: Microsoft's setup guidance grants AI Administrator and License Administrator editing of policies, limits, alerts and billing methods but not policy creation.
claims.quote: AI administrator and License administrator roles can edit spending policies, manage limits and alerts, and billing methods. However, they can't create spending policies.

claims.claim: AI Reader, Global Reader and supported reader roles can view consumption without policy-configuration permissions.
claims.quote: These roles provide read-only access to consumption information and don't allow administrators to create or change spending policies, limits, alerts, request policies, or billing methods.

claims.claim: The setup page inconsistently also lists License Administrator among read-only consumption roles.
claims.quote: AI Reader, Global Reader, License Administrator, and other supported reader-based roles can view consumption dashboards and reports. These roles provide read-only access to consumption information

claims.claim: An existing Power Platform role does not itself become a Microsoft 365 role for Copilot Studio cost management.
claims.quote: The recommendations are role assignments to consider; an existing Power Platform role does not itself become a Microsoft 365 role.

claims.claim: Alerts notify rather than enforce spending limits.
claims.quote: Configure notify-only threshold alerts and manage their recipients.

claims.claim: Alert emails start at the configured threshold and repeat daily until the monthly period resets or the policy is adjusted.
claims.quote: Alert emails begin when usage reaches the specified threshold and continue daily until the monthly usage period resets or you adjust the spending policy.

claims.claim: Deleting a policy does not remove, reallocate or reset Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: Deleting a spending policy doesn't remove, reallocate, or reset Copilot Credits.

claims.claim: After deletion, users can continue under another policy that applies through their group membership.
claims.quote: If another spending policy applies to a user through group membership, the user continues to consume Copilot Credits under the applicable policy.

claims.claim: The Cost Management Overview tab refreshes every four hours.
claims.quote: The **Overview** tab refreshes every 4 hours.

claims.claim: The Consumption tab refreshes every two hours.
claims.quote: The **Consumption** tab refreshes every 2 hours.

claims.claim: Consumption reports by policy, user, group, agent and service and includes limit utilisation.
claims.quote:
The **Consumption** tab provides reporting experiences for copilot credit usage by:

- Spending policy
- User
- Group
- Agent
- Service

**Limit utilization**: Credit usage divided by the current spending limit.

claims.claim: Administrators review submitted requests on the Credit requests page.
claims.quote: To view and approve credit requests from end users, select **View requests**. The **Credit requests** page displays all pending and approved requests.

claims.claim: The reviewed Microsoft documentation gives no PowerShell cmdlet for spending policies.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot" "spending policies" "PowerShell"; "spending policies" "resource" "Graph" PowerShell. Read returned excerpts and opened Cost Management overview, create, update and Studio costs. No spending-policy PowerShell cmdlet was documented.

claims.claim: The reviewed guidance states the 12-minute allowance for resource-policy linking, not for changes to identity-policy limits.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot identity spending policy limit changes take effect delay. Opened manage credits, Studio costs and Graph update; read search excerpts. Identity creation applies immediately, but no identity-limit-edit delay is stated. Studio linking has the 12-minute allowance.
